method: Read each Gemini <slug>.md dossier + world_reefs_master.json entry for the 13 mapped reefs, diffed against our verified <slug>.json cards. A sample of Gemini's candidate quotes/facts were independently re-fetched via WebSearch/WebFetch in this session (no subagent-spawning tool was available in this environment, so verification was done directly rather than via separate spawned agents) to confirm they are real before being offered as trustworthy. Items that could not be independently confirmed, or that were contradicted by the real source, are marked verified:false / verified:"contradicted" and must NOT be used without further checking.

candidate_facts.value: Gemini's dossier adds a rolled-up figure not in our card: 'Total lifecycle expenditure ~AUD $4.5M+' (original build AUD $2.3M + 2018 renewal AUD $2M). This is just Gemini's own addition of two figures already in our card, not an independently sourced new fact.
candidate_facts.note: Arithmetic derived, not a new sourced fact -- not worth adding.

contradictions.note: Minor institution-name mismatch (Delft Hydraulics Laboratory vs Delft University of Technology) -- low value, not independently re-verified.

per_reef.notes: Our existing card is already extremely thorough for this reef (looks like it was already reconciled against Gemini-style material once). All of Gemini's surfer/official reviews (linez, stunet, warddy, Fish Face, the-spleen_2, Tom Tate) are already present in our card, several verbatim. Nothing new survives scrutiny.

contradictions.field: Shaw Mead quote re: Opunake sandbags
contradictions.ours: "I understand it went over budget and no more funds were available, not a rare story for construction projects." (Newsroom NZ, 2021-12-06)
contradictions.gemini: "The sandbags were an evolutionary dead-end... We tried to get funding to cap the Opunake bags with rock to make it work, but the funding never came through."
contradictions.note: I fetched the real Newsroom NZ article ('The Kiwi scientist and the failed surf breaks', https://newsroom.co.nz/the-kiwi-scientist-and-the-failed-surf-breaks) directly. It contains the quote our card already uses, but does NOT contain the 'evolutionary dead-end' phrase or the rock-capping-funding-fell-through quote Gemini attributes to Mead. Likely a fabricated or misattributed quote by Gemini -- do not use.

contradictions.ours: "Today I heard an update on two of the recent failures..." (grouping Opunake with Bournemouth)
contradictions.gemini: "Ocean-based artificial reef attempts as a class have had absolutely horrible results. Millions of dollars have been poured into the ocean with virtually nothing to show for it..."
contradictions.note: Gemini cites this as from 'a global retrospective citing Opunake (2012)' with no URL. The Newsroom NZ article I fetched (Gemini's apparent implied source given the surrounding context) contains no Jim Moriarty quote at all. Treat Gemini's version as unverified/likely fabricated.

per_reef.notes: This reef is the clearest case where Gemini's material should NOT be trusted at face value: two of its four surfer/official quotes for Opunake do not appear in the article that, per its own citation pattern, should contain them. Recommend NOT importing any of Gemini's Opunake quotes beyond what our card already independently sourced.

per_reef.notes: Palm Beach's other Gemini quotes: the 'Gold Coast test surfer, Swellnet Dispatch 2019' quote could not be verified (Swellnet blocked WebFetch with 403; not independently confirmed -- do not use without another check). The 'ABC News Australia retrospective... 550,000 cubic meters' claim IS independently confirmed real (I fetched the actual ABC article, abc.net.au/news/2022-09-03/gold-coast-no-stranger-to-beach-erosion/101381812) but it is not a new fact -- our card's 'outcome' field already states 'ABC News reported approximately 550,000 m3 of sand retained over the reef's first two years' verbatim. Simon Mortensen's second Gemini quote ('we spent years refining computer models... learned every lesson from Narrowneck') is not in our card and not independently verified -- listed as unverified, not recommended for use without a source check.

candidate_refs.citation: Real Albany Advertiser article on the rock repositioning (found via WebSearch, not in Gemini's reference list): "Eighteen rocks of Southern Ocean Surf Reef repositioned in successful bid to reduce user injuries."
candidate_refs.supports: 18 boulders repositioned (matches Gemini's '18 boulders' claim), but WebFetch on this specific URL failed (connection reset) so the cost figure and full quotes could not be independently confirmed this session; a WebSearch summary separately suggested the repositioning cost was just over $20,000, not the $9 million Gemini's review section implies.

contradictions.ours: AUD $11.75 million 'Total Committed Funds' per City of Albany; Wikipedia/ABC/Beachgrit reported approx. AUD $13 million
contradictions.gemini: Review quote from 'Albany Boardriders Club spokesperson' claims 'over $9 million' in government backing; separately, Gemini's own body text states 'AUD $11.75M (~USD $7.8M)'
contradictions.note: I independently fetched the real ABC News article (abc.net.au/news/2025-07-16/southern-ocean-surf-reef-transforms-albany-wa/105530202). It states $10 million in combined 2017 state-government pledges ($5M from each major party) plus a further $5 million federal contribution in 2022 -- i.e. roughly $15M in pledged government funding, which matches neither Gemini's $9M review-quote figure nor its own $11.75M body-text figure exactly, though it is closer to our card's $11.75M-$13M range (which nets out state/federal/council/club contributions differently). The $9 million figure in Gemini's 'review' should be treated as unreliable/likely paraphrased poorly, not a verified new fact.

per_reef.notes: Both of Gemini's other Albany quotes (Peter Bolt, Cameron Warburton) were independently re-fetched from the real ABC News article and confirmed verbatim-accurate -- but both are already present in our card word-for-word, so nothing new. The 'Local Albany boardrider' ABC July 2025 quote and the BeachGrit quote could not be matched to any real article found via WebSearch (no BeachGrit article on this topic turned up); treat both as unverified. The Evan Watterson quote Gemini attributes to Albany ('performs far higher than the 41% design surfability target') is suspicious because the same name (with a different, real, independently-confirmed quote) appears as the Palm Beach reef's DHI engineer in Gemini's own palm-beach dossier and in our card -- possible name reuse/confusion by Gemini across two different reefs. Do not use this quote without confirming Evan Watterson actually worked on the Albany project too.
